chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Ammar ibn Hakim, from Abdul A'ala, the slave of the family of Saam, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, initiating:
The one who is unjust, Allah will set over him one who will oppress him (or upon his offspring), or upon the offspring of his offspring.
I said, 'He commits injustice and Allah sets [an oppressor] upon his offspring or upon the offspring of his offspring?' So he said:

Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is Saying: 'And let those fear who, should they leave behind them weakly offspring, would fear on their account, so let them fear Allah, and let them speak right words'.
ai.seo_question: How does divine justice affect the descendants of an unjust person according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the principle of *tadhiyyah* (divine appointment of an agent) where Allah may use a specific oppressor or even the unjust person's own descendants to exact retribution for their injustice. The Imam reinforces this by citing Quran 4:9, drawing a parallel between the fear of leaving weak offspring and the broader spiritual imperative to fear Allah and speak truthfully, thereby linking familial consequence to divine justice. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that injustice carries both immediate and generational repercussions, serving as a deterrent rooted in Quranic exhortation.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Ammar Bin Hakeym, from Abdul A’ala, a slave of the family of Saam who said,
‘The one who is unjust, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Overcome him with the one who would oppress him (or upon his offspring), or upon the offspring of his offspring’.

I said, ‘He commits injustice and Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Overcomes upon his offspring or upon the offspring of his offspring?’ So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said:

‘Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying: [4:9] And let those fear who, should they leave behind them weakly offspring, would fear on their account, so let them fear Allah, and let them speak right words’.
en.sarwar: 13. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ibn abu Najaran from ‘Ammar ibn Hakim from ‘Abd al-‘Ala’ Mawla Ale Sam who has said the following: “
Once abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) on his own initiation said, ‘
Whoever does injustice, Allah makes someone to dominate him or his descendents of first or second generations.’
I then asked, ‘It is he who has done injustice, how will Allah make his descendents suffer?’ The Imam said, ‘

Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, says, “Those who are concerned about the welfare of their own children after their death, should have fear of Allah (when dealing with the orphans) and guide them properly.’” [4:9]
